title: Abdominal Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute abdominal/back pain, fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine (hemoglobinuria) following exposure to an oxidative stressor (fava beans, infection, certain drugs: sulfa, primaquine, dapsone, nitrofurantoin, rasburicase). Labs show acute hemolytic anemia (low Hb, elevated LDH, low haptoglobin, elevated reticulocyte count, indirect hyperbilirubinemia). Peripheral smear shows bite cells, blister cells, and Heinz bodies. G6PD deficiency is the most common enzymopathy worldwide — X-linked recessive. G6PD protects RBCs from oxidative stress. Trigger → oxidative damage → intravascular + extravascular hemolysis. Diagnosis: G6PD enzyme assay (do NOT check during acute hemolysis — reticulocytes have higher G6PD). Treatment: supportive — remove trigger, IV fluids, transfuse if severe anemia. Avoid oxidative drugs lifelong. Screen family members (X-linked).
chief_complaint: Acute abdominal pain, jaundice, dark urine
